subject: FinLytics — post-demo: architecture notes, routing policies, and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Patel <spatel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jan 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: FinLytics — post-demo: architecture notes, routing policies, and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can line up a technical POC: 

Call recap (high-level)
- Primary use case: real-time semantic search + result re-ranking for FinLytics’ insights dashboard (low tail-latency for top-k retrieval).
- Key constraints: sub-150ms 95th percentile for query-only responses, EU data residency for subset of customers, and procurement window target = end of Q1.
- Team: you (Platform lead), Aisha (procurement), engineering (will own POC), plus Redwood solutions (Marissa) and AE (me).

Open technical priorities we agreed to validate in POC
1) Auth & tokens: short-lived credentials + SSO integration (Okta) — confirm if token rotation + scoped keys are required for POC.
2) SDK and early integration: embed search pipeline using our JS/Python SDKs; prefer server-side embed/rerank to keep keys in a service.
3) Model routing + policy: route high-priority interactive queries to lower-latency but higher-cost models, fall back to cheaper variants under contention; region routing to US-EAST (primary) / EU-WEST (residency users).
4) Embeddings + reranker: plan to use embeddings for recall + lightweight reranker for top-10 to meet latency targets.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Marissa to run a 60–90 minute integration deep-dive with your engineering team next week (suggest Tue/Wed).
- I’ll share a POC map and an architecture sketch (attached) showing where Redwood SDK and routing policy hooks live.
- FinLytics to confirm priority order: latency vs cost vs residency (we discussed latency > residency > cost, but please confirm).

Attachments: redwood-arch-sketch.png (high-level), routing-policy-template.json (example), POC-MAP-2026-01.xlsx (timeline/responsibilities).

If that list looks right, can you confirm 2–3 times for a technical session and whether Aisha should be on the procurement cadence call?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <spatel@finlytics.com>

Cc: Aisha Kaur <aisha@finlytics.com>, Platform Team <platform@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: FinLytics — post-demo: architecture notes, routing policies, and next steps

Dylan — thanks for the summary and attachments. Accurate and helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

Priorities:
- Top: latency for interactive UX (we need P95 < 150ms for query only).
- Next: data residency — EU-WEST must be enforced for EU customer data.
- Cost: important but second-order; we’ll expect guidance on expected per-query $ estimates for different routing choices.

Auth/Provisioning:
- We use Okta for SSO. For the POC, scoped API keys that can be rotated programmatically are acceptable, but for production we’ll need SSO + short-lived tokens with automatic rotation. Can Redwood support an STS-style short-lived credential or OIDC-based flows for dedicated/private deployments?

POC scope & timeline:
- POC: integrate embeddings + a top-k reranker into our search service; validate latency, throughput, and cost for a ~100k monthly query volume.
- Procurement: Aisha will lead contracting; target is the end of Q1 but we may accelerate based on POC results.

For the technical session, Tue 20 Jan 10:00–11:30 PST or Wed 21 Jan 13:00–14:30 PST work for our engineers. Aisha will join procurement portions.

Samir
VP Platform — FinLytics

Samir / Dylan — thanks, quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so your engineers have context. I’ll demo these during the session but wanted to surface specifics: 

1) SDK & quickstart
- For server-side POC: use the Python SDK. Example (pseudo):

# Python SDK snippet
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<SCOPED_KEY>")
resp = client.text.generate(model="gm-small", input="…")

- For embeddings: client.embeddings.create(model="embed-v1", input=["doc text"])
- We recommend doing embeddings offline and storing vector DB (we can point to best-practice Vector DB adapters).

2) Auth patterns
- Hosted: standard API keys + optional Okta/OIDC SCIM for user provisioning.
- Dedicated/Private: we support short-lived STS tokens integrated with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping; token rotation via our control-plane hooks. For the POC scoped API keys are fine; for production we’ll help set up OIDC flows.

3) Routing + policy examples
- Routing knobs: latency_target_ms, cost_ceiling_per_1000_tokens, region_preference, fallback_chain.
- Example policy (pseudo-JSON shown as reference):
{
  "routes": [
    {"name":"interactive","latency_target_ms":120,"preferred_models":["gm-lowlat","gm-medium"],"fallback_chain":["gm-small"]},
    {"name":"background","latency_target_ms":1000,"preferred_models":["gm-small"],"fallback_chain":[]}
  ],
  "region_routing": {"EU":"eu-west-1","US":"us-east-1"}
}

This will be part of what I walk through; policy is stored as a config file and can be applied per-route or per-customer.

4) Embeddings & reranker design
- Suggest: recall with embeddings (ANN search), fetch top-50, run a light-weight reranker model (gm-small or gm-mini) on top-10. That design keeps latency predictable and cost bounded.

5) Batching & KV cache
- If you expect bursts we’ll configure short window batching for background jobs and prefix caching for repeated queries to lower cost. For interactive queries we keep batch windows tiny to preserve latency.

I’ll include the routing-policy-template.json in the invite and walk through mapping your SLAs to these knobs. See attached sketch for where SDK calls live relative to your edge service.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <spatel@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: FinLytics — post-demo: architecture notes, routing policies, and next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful. Two follow-ups before the session: 

1) Fallback and QoS chaining: can Redwood enforce a soft SLA that routes to a cheaper model when cost ceiling is hit, but still guarantees a response (albeit lower-quality) within SLA window? We want predictable degradation, not hard failures.

2) Cost controls: can we set per-route daily spend caps and get alerts when thresholds are approaching? That’s important for procurement sign-off.

If both are supported, please flag any limitations for the hosted offering vs Dedicated/Private.

Samir
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Patel <spatel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodai.com>

Subject: Re: FinLytics — post-demo: architecture notes, routing policies, and next steps (answers + POC plan)

Samir — short answers then schedule:

- Fallback / graceful degradation: yes. You can configure fallback chains that prefer low-latency models and fall back to cheaper variants if capacity or cost thresholds hit. Policy can be "soft" (prefer but allow) or "hard" (block). We’ll demo a soft fallback that preserves response availability while trading quality.
- Cost controls: yes. Per-route daily/weekly spend caps + alerts (we tie into Slack/email and also surface in Console). For Dedicated we can also build custom billing hooks for more granular spend tracking.

POC plan (owners, timeline):
- Redwood: Marissa (technical), Jordan (routing policy + Optimize), Dylan (engage / contracting).
- FinLytics: Samir (platform lead), Eng lead (TBD), Aisha (procurement).
- Milestones:
  - Week 0: alignment + architecture sketch (done).
  - Week 1: provisioning test keys, baseline latency test with gm-small.
  - Week 2: embeddings pipeline + reranker integration.
  - Week 3: routing policy tuning and cost runs.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 20 Jan 10:00–11:30 PST (holds both options). Please accept/adjust. I’ll include the routing-policy-template.json and the POC MAP in the invite.

Pricing note: I’ll share an initial cost estimate in the meeting; for the POC we commonly provide a credit buffer while you validate production metrics.

Thanks,
Dylan
